creem.activation_decision_2026-09-05: NOT activating now, despite approval. Creem's role is Merchant-of-Record payment/checkout infrastructure -- the same job Stripe already does live for this experiment (prod_V8TDzCnDU7y2r9, $19, Managed Payments + automatic tax). Approval removes the 'is it usable' uncertainty but does not create a Net-Profit case on its own: no buyer would newly discover the product through Creem (it has no marketplace/search surface, unlike Etsy or Gumroad), so building it would only offer existing buyers a second checkout for the same product -- pure substitution, not incremental reach. Building it now would cost real AI-compute (product config, checkout integration, workflow, docs, cost-ledger wiring) for zero expected incremental revenue, while Etsy (validated buyer search-intent, going live this same iteration) and watching Gumroad/Etsy for a first sale are both higher-expected-value uses of the same budget. Would reconsider only if a specific advantage over Stripe surfaces (e.g. materially lower fees, a market/currency Stripe can't serve, or a partner/embed distribution channel unique to Creem) -- none identified as of this decision.
creem.assessment: Even with account + API + approval all confirmed, Creem's role is Merchant-of-Record payment/billing infrastructure -- functionally the same job Stripe already does live, not a marketplace with its own buyer-search discovery. No distribution-value differentiator over Stripe has been identified. Deprioritized: approved and usable, but NOT being activated absent a specific identified advantage (would be redundant payment infra).

latest_strategy_decision_ja: 前回の結論を擁護するのではなく、根本の誤りを訂正した：Pages自体に訪問者がいない場合、未検証の導線ステップ（Pages→Etsy）の修正を『流入問題を解決した』とみなすことはできず、『買い手はEtsyにいる』という主張は診断を装った仮定に過ぎなかった。オーナーの明示的な優先順位に従い、Pages側の追加作業よりも各チャネル自身の実データ（APIレスポンス、Stripeライブクエリ）による検証を選んだ。露出ブーストの主張は、Etsy公式ドキュメントでも実測データでも確認されていないため、事実ではなく明示的な未検証の仮説として扱った——約7時間でviewsがゼロなのは『判断にはまだ早い』とも『ブーストは存在しない』とも整合し、どちらか一方を選ぶのは不誠実である。今回とった行動（観測のみ）は、リソース再配分を正当化する実シグナルがまだ無いことを反映している。唯一確認できた推測ではない欠陥（Gumroadの『Other』カテゴリ）は、それが証拠に基づいているからこそ次の具体的な修正候補として位置づけた——今チャネル間のリソース再配分を判断するのとは対照的に。
latest_strategy_decision_en: Corrected the underlying error rather than defend the prior conclusion: a fix to an unproven funnel step (Pages->Etsy) cannot be credited with solving inflow if Pages itself has no visitors, and 'Etsy is where the buyers are' was an assumption dressed as a diagnosis. Chose to verify with each channel's own real data (API responses, live Stripe query) over further Pages work, per the owner's explicit priority order. Treated the recency-boost claim as an explicit open hypothesis rather than a fact, since neither Etsy's official docs nor measured data confirm it -- ~7h of zero views is consistent with either 'too early to tell' or 'no boost exists,' and it would be dishonest to pick one. The one action taken (none this turn beyond observation) reflects that no real signal yet justifies reallocating resources; the one confirmed, non-speculative defect found (Gumroad's 'Other' category) is queued as the next concrete fix precisely because it is evidence-backed, unlike a channel-reallocation call would be right now.

Chose the owned-asset backlink fix over every other candidate lever specifically because it was the only one backed by concrete evidence of an actual gap (verified via grep, not assumed) rather than speculation: price/product-mix changes have no evidence current pricing is the blocker; a 2nd SKU is more work with no signal yet to justify it; X posting is dormant (no credentials, zero posts ever sent) so acting on it would have zero real-world effect right now. Etsy was prioritized over further Gumroad/Stripe asset work because it's the only channel with validated organic search demand AND is in its highest-visibility window as a brand-new listing -- the same backlink fix on Gumroad or Stripe would have lower expected marginal value. Explicitly declined to add a 4th sales channel: none of the 3 live channels has shown a structural (not merely early-stage) limit that would justify one, so doing so now would violate the standing 'don't build new capability without a confirmed constraint' discipline.

human_actions_required.why_ai_cannot: Investigated first, per instruction, before asking: confirmed via Gumroad's own production source that view/traffic data is served only by a session-cookie-authenticated web controller (AnalyticsController < Sellers::BaseController), not the OAuth v2 API this project's access token uses -- the documented API scopes (edit_products, view_sales, view_profile, mark_sales_as_shipped, refund_sales) contain no analytics/views scope, and the live GET /v2/products/:id response (scripts/gumroad_listing_diagnostics.mjs) confirms no views field exists on that resource either. This sandbox also has zero egress to gumroad.com regardless. Genuinely not AI-reachable, not merely unconfirmed -- hence exactly one human-only ask, not a recurring one.

additional_permissions_requested.purpose: Optional monitoring capability, not a payment prerequisite — Stripe checkout already works without it. It lets sales-monitor.yml (GitHub Actions) poll Stripe every 4h and detect revenue even in the hours a Routine session isn't running.
